issues.what: Inner-fold over-purge for learner B's p* selection (and the same helper used by A): fold_masks purges training trades whose trajectory intersects [min(block start), max(block end)] over the test blocks. For the non-contiguous inner folds `tr_blocks[i::3]` this range spans the blocks in between, so every trade in those blocks is purged and the inner training set collapses to a single block for 2 of 3 inner folds (1m: 250-492 trades instead of the intended ~5 blocks; 5m: 47-82 trades). p* is therefore chosen on badly under-trained inner models. Not a leak (it is conservative), and B is not a candidate, but FINDINGS' 'p* by an inner 3-fold on the training fold' over-states the procedure that actually ran.
issues.evidence: Reproduced: outer fold 0 (1m) inner test blocks [4,7,10] -> inner train n 492 from blocks [11] (intended [5,6,8,9,11]); [5,8,11] -> n 361 from [4]; outer fold 2 [0,3,6] -> n 250 from [7]. 5m: [0,3,6] -> n 47 from [7]; [4,7,10] -> n 82 from [11].
issues.fix: Purge per test block (loop over blocks exactly as harness._purge does) or use contiguous inner folds; re-run 03_b_imitation.py and state the inner training sizes in FINDINGS.

Exact-replay claim confirmed and strengthened: the numba floor equals the lab.manage Foundation-stop-only variant (grid col 1176) on EVERY trade (exit bar identical, max |net diff| 0.0) on both timeframes; a fresh lab.manage call on 300 random trades per tf gives 0 mismatches; every trajectory stays in its entry session (so harness purge by the L1 exit bar is equivalent to purge by the variant's exit); lab.manage's cap is the entry day's 15:25 (lab.py:932-933), matching the FINDINGS cap definition; price_np == lab.price_trade holds on all 4452/826 stop-or-cap fills. In-sample best = variant 1176 (1m, -904.77, 226 above Foundation) / 1024 (5m, -648.81, 173 above). The top 45 per-trade gains sum to 682,848 INR against a total diff sum of 385,417, so the 'few runners' description is accurate. Exit ledger: 3173 rows = 3173 unique ids = 3173 vector files (per tf 1568 C + 11 CPCV + 4 comparators + C_nested + C_best_is + B, plus A on 5m). SPA/PBO family = the 1568 C variants; SPA best is variant 785 (stop 75, CHoCH on, t 1.683) -> p 0.396; the nested pick's own session-equal-weighted gain is +31.4 INR/trade (t 0.55, unadjusted one-sided p 0.29), so the family-wide SPA failure is not an artefact. issues.what: The family SPA p-values reported as the multiplicity verdict are inflated by an implementation artifact: harness.spa studentises every candidate, and variant 1177 (foundation stop + exit_on_choch_against, which equals the L1 benchmark on all but 8 of 4,452 minute trades / 1 of 826 five-minute trades; per-session gain sd 6.5 INR on minute, 40 INR on 5m) produces a heavy-tailed bootstrap statistic that attains the family max in 302/2000 RC and 396/2000 SPA draws on minute and 755/2000 on 5-minute (its statistic exceeds 17,000 in 37% of 5m draws). Removing the near-duplicates of the benchmark: minute SPA p 0.396 -> 0.322 (RC 0.501 -> 0.448); 5-minute SPA p 0.4965 -> 0.165 (RC 0.5175 -> 0.191; 0.1015 when the 34 variants differing from the benchmark in < 100 sessions are removed). Both remain above the 0.10 threshold, so the FAIL on SPA and the null verdict stand, but the reported 5-minute figure is ~3x the family's true p and the same artifact will affect any harness family that contains a near-copy of its benchmark.

issues.fix: Report the SPA p over the family with exact or near-duplicates of the benchmark removed (or floor the studentising sd at a sensible fraction of the benchmark's per-session sd) and state both numbers; flag in harness.py that spa() must not receive candidates whose gain series is a rounding-noise copy of the benchmark. The verdict does not change.

issues.what: The pass-rule check 'diff_top1_gains_removed > 0' is not the pre-registered statistic. BRIEF, README rule 5 and harness.metrics define 'the difference with the top 1% winners removed' (trades whose net is in the top 1%); the study instead removes the top 1% of per-trade policy-minus-Foundation gains, a one-sided trim that is biased negative for any heavy-tailed series (applied to the sign-flipped series it gives -162; the symmetric 1%/1% trim gives +7.46). The pre-registered version, computed by the study itself as diff_top1_winners_removed, is +4.01 (pass) but is omitted from FINDINGS.md's table and from the pass rule. 06_findings.py's docstring states the pass rule was written after learner C's results were read. The 'no candidate' verdict is unaffected because SPA fails regardless (and under the harness GO the book also fails kept_mean_slip8 > 0 at -1313 and DSR p 1.0), but the FINDINGS attribute the failure to a post-hoc metric.

issues.what: Learner B's inner 3-fold for p* uses interleaved inner test blocks (tr_blocks[i::3]) with a purge over the min..max bar range of those blocks, which removes every block lying between them: the inner training sets are a single block (250-492 trades on minute, 47-82 on 5-minute) instead of ~5 blocks. Not a leak (conservative) and B is not a candidate, but p* is chosen from a model fit on ~10% of the outer training fold, which explains 'never exit' in 2 of 3 minute folds and adds noise the design did not intend.
issues.evidence: Reproduced with controls_minute.npz J and the harness block ranges: minute outer fold 0 inner training sets 492 (block 11) / 361 (block 4) / 1387 (blocks 4,5,10,11) trades out of 2,746; 5-minute outer fold 2 inner training 47 / 82 / 287 out of 556.
issues.fix: Use contiguous inner blocks (e.g. consecutive triples) or purge per test block rather than over the min-max span; report inner training sizes.

issues.what: The random-exit control cannot discriminate any stop-based policy from the benchmark: the Foundation L1 exit itself scores 97.0 (>= 95) on minute and 96.8 on 5-minute against a no-stop uniform-bar exit, so the pass-rule check 'random_pct >= 95' is vacuous for a policy-vs-Foundation comparison. The design panel specified this control and the study reports it honestly beside every policy, but its 'pass' carries no evidence.
